A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HandSCS and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references supporting reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to separate supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v2 reports original InterHand2.6M rendering results, quantitative component ablations, qualitative comparisons, and a 58 FPS inference result.

after.justification: v3 reports original rendering results across five subjects, component and coordinate-space ablations, and PCA and t-SNE feature visualizations.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming dynamic bones as virtual bones, v3 changes cross-pose matching from spatial positions to SCS coordinates. It replaces EMA-cached consistency targets with previous-iteration attributes and embeddings, introduces raw radial distance for virtual bones instead of the shared exponential weighting, and replaces geometry-embedding smoothness with offset regularization (Sections 3.1–3.3). These change the representation and training procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds novel-pose evaluation under limited-view and limited-pose observations on train/Capture5 and train/Capture6 (Section 4.1 and Figure 4). This extends observation conditions within the retained InterHand2.6M right-hand domain; the existing novel-pose and novel-view tasks remain.

E2.justification: 3DGS-Avatar is added to both quantitative novel-pose and novel-view comparisons in v3 Tables 1–2 and to the qualitative pose comparison. HandAvatar, LiveHand, and GauHuman remain. The newly cited hand-avatar works are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Novel-pose evaluation expands from three to five subjects, and new experiments introduce regularizer and canonical-versus-posed-space controls. The reported pose-similarity decay changes from 1.5 to 1.3. Rendering metrics and the 10-training-view/15-test-view protocol remain. The newly stated 5 FPS dataset rate does not establish a change from v2's unstated rate.

E4.justification: v3 adds a regularizer-only control in Table 3, canonical-versus-posed virtual-bone construction in Table 5, PCA comparisons of embeddings/LBS/SCS in Figure 1, and anatomical feature-clustering analysis in Figure 8. These substantially expand analysis of the representation's structural behavior beyond the retained component, bone-basis, and endpoint ablations.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Subject averages and the added result rows do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for two sparse-observation subjects, 3DGS-Avatar, and new analyses while retaining the original three subjects' novel-pose scores. Reported HandSCS novel-view PSNR changes from 35.31/35.45/35.77 to 35.18/35.41/35.74. New Table 1 shows LiveHand exceeding HandSCS in SSIM on both added subjects. The endpoint-ablation baseline changes from 0.9638/0.0334 to 0.9636/0.0335 for SSIM/LPIPS. The 58 FPS result disappears with the replaced opening figure.

T1.justification: Core mathematical definitions are revised: v3 separates radial descriptors by bone type, replaces spatial nearest-neighbor correspondence with structural-coordinate minimization, revises the consistency target, and explicitly defines an offset-norm regularizer (Equations 6–7, 11–12, and 14). These are substantive formal changes, although neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 presents SCS primarily as intra-pose guidance alongside a separate inter-pose loss. v3 extends its claimed role to a common structural representation governing both deformation and cross-pose correspondence, with residual embeddings included in the contribution statement. The overarching hand-animation, state-of-the-art, and real-time claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of why canonical virtual bones complement posed static bones, why raw distances provide broader descriptor range, and how feature clustering supports structural interpretation. It removes v2's explicit limitation concerning inaccurate MANO initialization and residual rendering failures. Existing static/virtual-bone tradeoffs and the interpretation of LiveHand's novel-view SSIM advantage remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-repository URL instead of promising release upon acceptance and newly specifies 5 FPS data. Conversely, it omits v2's ROM03/ROM04/ROM07 sequence names and explicit decoder-input equations, referring decoder details to unavailable supplementary material. Decoder widths, MANO initialization, and A100 evaluation hardware remain documented. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to interaction-aware one-shot hand avatars, JGHand, and t-SNE. Its introduction broadens the critique of earlier representations from global pose conditioning to LBS refinement and latent-code ambiguity. Most related-work discussion and the central structure-aware positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, substantial method explanations, ablation discussion, and conclusion are rewritten around SCS as a structural representation. Subsection terminology changes, including dynamic-to-virtual bones and intra-pose consistency, and an acknowledgement section is added. This is extensive narrative revision beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document from two columns to one, replaces Figure 1 with comparison/PCA panels, redesigns Figure 4 with detail crops and observation-condition groups, and adds Figure 8. The former combined benchmark table becomes separate pose/view tables, with an additional coordinate-space ablation table. Retained figures and tables are resized and rearranged throughout.

improvement.justification: The added 3DGS-Avatar comparison and targeted coordinate-space and feature analyses provide better support for the central structural-representation argument. This is a limited net improvement: v3 removes the MANO-failure limitation and 58 FPS evidence, makes some implementation details less self-contained, and leaves inaccurate result summaries. In particular, its claim of winning all novel-pose metrics conflicts with LiveHand's higher SSIM on both added subjects in Table 1.
